title: The verb and its preposition
description: Say what you depend on, what you insist on, and what you dream of.

explanation.summary: Many Spanish verbs come with a preposition, and the preposition is part of the verb. You cannot leave it out, and you cannot change it. This is one of the places where Spanish and English stop matching.

sections.heading: Verbs that look different in English
sections.body: Insistir takes en in Spanish and in on in English: insistir en algo. Soñar takes con: soñar con ser padre. Depender takes de: depender de la suerte. Jugar takes a: jugar al fútbol. Some verbs use the same preposition as English: pensar en, hablar de, depender de.

sections.heading: Asking about the link
sections.body: When the verb and the preposition come apart, the preposition is what you ask about. Depender de becomes en qué depende, and soñar con becomes con qué sueñas. This is why the preposition is worth learning as its own word.

examples.en: He insists on doing it himself.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: Some verbs take a fixed preposition: depender de, insistir en, soñar con.

exercises.prompt: Pick the Spanish word for “to depend”.
exercises.note: It always takes de: depender de algo.

exercises.prompt: Pick the Spanish word for “to insist”.
exercises.note: It always takes en: insistir en algo.

exercises.prompt: Pick the Spanish word for “to dream”.
exercises.note: It always takes con: soñar con algo.
The preposition is what you ask about.

exercises.prompt: Me di ___ de que era tarde.
